Subject: Notification: downstream delegation for EdgeWave logging connector

Hi David —

Quick heads up from VendorCo: our EdgeWave logging connector is onboarding a subcontractor (LogStream Inc.) that will handle log parsing and short-term storage for 30 days while we process ingestion. Per our MSA with Acme / Redwood, we wanted to notify you and get written consent for the downstream delegation + the DPA annex that covers limited retention and encryption-in-transit.

I attached the proposed DPA redlines and a one-page subcontractor matrix. Key points: LogStream will have access to normalized logs but will not receive customer identifiers; retention is set to 30 days; we propose AES-256 at rest and TLS1.3 in transit. They asked to be added as an authorized subprocessor by June 10 to meet their ramp.

Please confirm whether Redwood requires any additional controls (audit log access, attestations) before you can sign off. Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Elli Son

David / team —

I reviewed the DPA redlines. High-level comments:
1) Narrow the processing purpose language to "log parsing and transient storage for the purposes of ingestion validation and format normalization" — current draft is broader.
2) Add a requirement for an annual third-party security assessment or, alternatively, provision of LogStream's most recent SOC 2 report before access is granted.
3) Change the retention clause to say "maximum 30 days unless retention is required by law; any retention >7 days must be flagged and auditable by Redwood."
4) Require contractual right to access subprocessor logs related to Redwood traffic and right to terminate access on 5 days' notice for critical findings.

Operational asks: we need the exact IAM role/name LogStream will use and the minimal network CIDR ranges for firewall allowlist. Also we want a copy of LogStream's dataflow diagram.

Elli — please ask LogStream to accept the above points; if they push back we can propose a compensating control (e.g., continuous audit webhook) but that will take more time to vet.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference

Elli — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping Rita (Acme). Per Kimberly's review above, we need LogStream to accept a narrow processing purpose, provide SOC2 or equivalent evidence, and agree to the "flagging" and audit access language (see Kimberly's bullets 1-4).

Next steps I propose:
1) VendorCo asks LogStream to confirm in writing on company letterhead that they will not perform PII enrichment and that they accept the processing purpose and retention guardrails.
2) VendorCo uploads LogStream's SOC2 (or ISO) report to the Drive link I shared and confirms the IAM role / IP CIDR.
3) Legal will prepare a short DPA annex with the 5-day termination clause and the audit access language; I'll circulate a DocuSign envelope for VendorCo + LogStream + Acme to execute.

Can you aim to get steps 1-2 done by end of day Monday 2027-05-31 so we can route the annex and DocuSign before your onboarding deadline? If LogStream cannot provide SOC2, propose an alternative timeline and compensating control.

If needed, Marissa and I can host a 30-minute triage call Friday morning to unblock technical questions.

Best,
David
